injuryReport.name: P.J. Locke
injuryReport.shortComment: Locke suffered a concussion during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
injuryReport.longComment: Locke was able to clear concussion protocol and play in Week 9 after suffering a concussion in Week 8 against the Cardinals. The safety now appears to have picked up a concussion in a second straight game. Locke will have an uphill battle to be available for Week 10 against the 49ers, and if he misses that contest, Markquese Bell would be a top candidate to draw the start at strong safety.
factors: Remains in early stages of NFL 5-Step Concussion Protocol

injuryReport.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuryReport.shortComment: Schoonmaker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's clash against the Colts.
injuryReport.longComment: Schoonmaker continues to tend to a groin issue and will miss his second straight game. He did manage a trio of limited practices during the week, so the tight end may be able to play next Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco. Dallas' tight-end corps will consist of Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell in Week 9.

injuryReport.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuryReport.shortComment: Mingo (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injuryReport.longComment: Mingo was hurt in the second half and may not be able to return to the game. Prior to his exit, he caught one of three targets for 23 yards. With George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, the Cowboys will be down to CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson at wideout if Mingo can't return.

injuryReport.name: George Pickens
injuryReport.shortComment: Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.
injuryReport.longComment: For a second week in a row, Pickens endured practice restrictions due to a hamstring injury, leaving him questionable to suit up in Week 9. On Friday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site that he was "hopeful" Pickens would be available this weekend, but that didn't come to pass. With Pickens and fellow WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson will compose Dallas' receiving corps.

irReserve.name: Jalen Thompson
irReserve.beatNote: Thompson is still working his way back from a hamstring injury that forced the team to place him on injured reserve in late September, and he is not ready to return to practice quite yet. In his absence, P.J. Locke (concussion), Malik Hooker and Markquese Bell are poised to continue to operate as the Cowboys' primary safeties.

irReserve.name: Jonathan Bullard
irReserve.beatNote: Bullard had his practice window opened Oct. 29 and was a full participant in all three of the Cowboys' practices this week. However, he's not yet ready to return to game action. Bullard's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco.

irReserve.name: Malachi Lawrence
irReserve.beatNote: Lawrence suffered an ankle injury last Sunday in a loss to Arizona and had already been ruled out for Week 9. The move to IR means he'll need to miss at least three additional games, so the earliest Lawrence can return is Monday, Dec. 7, against Seattle. The Cowboys activated fellow linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) from IR on Saturday to fill Lawrence's roster spot.

irReserve.name: Malik Davis
irReserve.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irReserve.beatNote: Davis underwent surgery Saturday for a hip injury, and Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports that the procedure will sideline the 27-year-old running back for the entire 2026 season. With Davis on the shelf, the Cowboys bolstered their backfield depth by signing Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster, with the latter serving as the RB3 behind Javonte Williams and Emari Demercado.
